We developed automobiles — and improved safety along the way.

item.title: Letter: Near-miss hurricanes as instructive as direct hits
item.dc:creator: None
item.description: The Star-Advertiser’s Sept. 27 story, “Big sigh of relief,” will be filed as good news, and the costs of Hurricane Nolo’s near-miss will never be fully counted. But they are real: closed parks and highways, emptied rooms, staff sent home, emergency crews mobilized. This is Hawaii’s second cyclone scare in weeks, and each one bills the visitor economy without producing many headlines about losses.

item.title: Kokua Line: Does gift-card law apply to national chains in Hawaii?
item.dc:creator: Christine Donnelly
item.description: Question: I visited a national coffee chain on Oahu and paid with a gift card. After my purchase, the remaining balance was under $4. When I asked for the balance in cash, the employee told me the store does not give cash back on gift cards. I mentioned the Hawaii law (HRS §481B‑13(c)), which requires businesses in Hawaii to redeem gift card balances under $5 for cash. The employee said this law does not apply to national chains. I don’t believe that’s correct. My understanding is that any business operating in Hawaii must follow this law, regardless of whether it’s a national or local company. Can you clarify whether this law applies to national chains operating in Hawaii?

item.title: Editorial: Use student harm registry diligently
item.dc:creator: None
item.description: For any parent or guardian of a school-aged child, the growing accusations of sexual predation by former Moanalua High School wrestling coach Sean S. Sakaida, 44, are chilling to hear. Sakaida has been charged by the FBI with receipt and possession of child pornography, stemming from an alleged improper sexual relation with a wrestling student, age 17; meanwhile, other disturbing incidents from his past, while employed by the public school system, are starting to surface. Sakaida remains in custody pending a preliminary hearing, and it will be up to a federal court to find him innocent or guilty.
